title: How can my AI agent help me avoid a Google stock crash
author: Proper_Bit_118
selftext:
A bear market is the real test for an AI investment system. I deeply know selling is actually much harder. When you sell and why you sell often determines whether you ultimately make money.

On November 27, my AI Agent completely sold all of its Google holdings, along with a detailed explanation of the reasons. The stock then dropped 12.29%. It perfectly avoided the decline!

The longer it runs and the more it learns, the better it gets. It doesn’t try to predict the market. 

It just tries to make the highest-probability risk/reward decision at any given time. In this case, five things specified why the AI agent fully exited Google:

*  **Relative strength severely lagging**: Over the past six months, it underperformed the tech sector by 28 percentage points. It fell 8.5% while the sector rose nearly 20%.
* **Valuation is not cheap**: PEG is elevated. The so-called “16x P/E” is partly an accounting illusion — some of the earnings come from non-operating income, so the true valuation is on the expensive side.
* **Cash flow is deteriorating**: Free cash flow yield is extremely low; most of the operating cash flow is being spent on capital expenditures.
* **Trend has broken**: It broke below key moving averages, a death cross is imminent, and capital is flowing out.
*  **Technicals continue to weaken**, with no bullish signals appearing.



After running this for about a year I’ve basically stopped trusting my own judgment on individual trades. I just pick the overall investment strategy and let the system handle the entries and exits.

In a bull market, AI can create the illusion that you can easily make money just by asking it which stocks to buy. In reality, a bear market is the real test for AI in investing. I’ve experienced multiple times where it helped me avoid drawdowns.

Have you ever handed your investment decisions over to AI? Let’s chat in the comments !
